page: OVHcloud a10-90 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 60 dedicated AMD EPYC 9554 physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 85 GB of system memory, 400 GB of local SSD storage, and 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The primary hardware highlight is the inclusion of two NVIDIA A10 Ampere GPUs, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU score, and Redis SET operations. It also demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference speeds across small, medium, and large models for both prompt processing and text generation. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and Geekbench image processing fall into the average category.

With 1.42 GB of RAM per core, the server presents a tradeoff: it offers massive parallel compute and GPU acceleration but is constrained in memory-heavy tasks. This resource density makes it highly cost-efficient for GPU-bound workloads like LLM inference, machine learning, and parallel compilation, while being less suitable for massive in-memory databases.
description: The OVHcloud a10-90 is a GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-intensive and parallel processing workloads. It features 60 dedicated AMD EPYC 9554 physical cores running at 3.3 GHz, paired with 85 GB of system memory and 400 GB of local SSD storage. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA A10 Ampere GPUs delivering 48 GB of combined VRAM. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, Redis operations, and LLM inference across various model sizes. However, with only 1.42 GB of RAM per core, the server exhibits a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, presenting a tradeoff for memory-heavy applications. It is highly cost-efficient for GPU-bound tasks, machine learning, and parallel compilation, but less suited for large in-memory databases.
